**Meridian Tidal Pilot - Final Operations Review Summary**

The primary equipment failure was **Turbine T-4**, which went offline on 14 March 2025 after its bearing seal corroded through, allowing seawater into the nacelle. The root cause was traced to corrosion of the bearing seal housing. This was the only failure causing a multi-week outage during the pilot.

Over the 24-month operating period, **18.7 GWh** was delivered to the grid, which was 6 percent below the original forecast of 19.9 GWh.

The project cost EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million — an overrun of EUR 4.55 million (12.4%), driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign.

**Environmental monitoring** showed no statistically significant change in fish migration counts after installation (p = 0.41).

**Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing titanium fasteners with duplex stainless steel** on all remaining nacelles, a change the steering group accepted in principle.

The **final decision** was that the steering group approved Phase 2 for Q3 2026, contingent on a completed bearing seal redesign and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
